subject: Quantum Health: tailored retention & erasure exception for debug logs
messages:
From: Laura Voss <lvoss@quantumhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Quantum Health Security <security@quantumhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Retention & erasure: customer-specific log policy for Quantum Health

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Security asked me to follow up with a quick set of questions around data retention for our account. We run a regulated workflow that requires:
- retention proof for debug/audit logs for 180 days,
- the ability to request targeted deletion for specific tenant IDs within a 30-day SLA, and
- a forensic snapshot export (syslog + request traces) if we open an audit within 7 days of an incident.

Attached is our SIG-derived questionnaire (named QuantumHealth_SIG_Questions.pdf) with the specific fields flagged. Can Redwood confirm:
1) whether you support a customer-scoped retention window longer than the default for debug logs;
2) the process and timeline to perform a targeted deletion and how you produce a proof-of-delete artifact; and
3) whether you can provide the 7-day forensic snapshot on short notice and what the expected delivery SLA and file format would be.

We're under an upcoming SOC2 readiness audit and need to document any exceptions or compensating controls by the end of next week. Appreciate any immediate clarification and an outline of the evidence you can provide.

Best,
Laura Voss
Head of Security Operations
Quantum Health

Attachment: QuantumHealth_SIG_Questions.pdf (pdf, 1 page)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Retention & erasure: customer-specific log policy for Quantum Health

Folks — forwarding Quantum Health's SIG questions (attached). High level asks: longer-than-default retention for debug logs (180d), targeted deletion SLA (30d), and a 7-day forensic snapshot export. Can we confirm feasibility and what evidence we can produce (proof-of-delete, export package contents, timestamps)?

Quick thoughts:
- From product/runtime side, we have tenant-scoped TTLs for ephemeral traces and configurable retention for debug logs, but longer windows may increase storage and cost — need infra input on retention policies per customer.
- Proof-of-delete: we can produce a signed manifest of deleted object ids and timestamps plus internal erasure job logs. Would that satisfy their auditor?
- Forensic snapshot: we can export request traces + syslog, but need to confirm retention granularity (are request traces indexed beyond 30d?) and whether we can guarantee a 7-day turnaround.

Olga — can you sketch what we can deliver and any caveats? Ben — legal/security: anything to watch re: regulatory or SLA risk if we agree to a 180d retention carveout? Priyom — please include CS process for a customer-triggered export (who coordinates, costs, approvals).

Thanks,
Diego

Attachment: QuantumHealth_SIG_Questions.pdf (pdf)

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T12:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Retention & erasure: customer-specific log policy for Quantum Health

Diego / team — summary of what we can provide and constraints: 

1) Customer-scoped retention (180 days)
- Technical: We support per-tenant retention configuration for debug/audit logs. Config is stored in the control plane and applied at ingestion. We can set a 180d TTL for the Quantum Health tenant.
- Caveats: Longer retention increases cost and requires a signed change order for Dedicated/Private or an approval for Hosted (billing adjustment). Also impacts snapshot/backup window.

2) Targeted deletion process (30-day SLA)
- We have a documented erasure workflow: receive SAR/request, validate tenant IDs and scope, schedule erasure job, purge objects from active stores, remove from hot KV caches, and then trigger background compaction to purge tombstoned data.
- Proof-of-delete artifacts we can produce: signed deletion manifest (object ids, tenant ids, timestamps), compaction job logs, and a signed statement from RedWood infra (sha256 checksums of manifest). We cannot provide raw binary traces of internal compaction processes but can provide hashed evidence.
- Timeline: Typical targeted deletion for a scoped tenant is 7-21 days in normal load; 30 days SLA is feasible with a formal request and CS acceptance window.

3) Forensic snapshot export (7-day request window)
- We can export request traces and related syslog entries as NDJSON (request-traces.ndjson, syslog.ndjson) plus an index manifest. Exports are generated from cold storage and may require 3–10 days to assemble depending on time range and size. We can commit to a 7-day SLA for up to a 72-hour time window per request with an approved acceleration fee for larger ranges.

Next steps / evidence pack: I prepared a short draft response to their SIG (sig_response_draft.docx) and a proposed export schedule template (proposed_export_schedule.csv). Also documenting control references: SOC2 CC6.1 (data retention) and our internal retention playbook (link below).

Technical caveats to call out in customer-facing answer:
- We will not guarantee raw debug binaries for confidentiality and platform integrity reasons; we provide exported artifacts and signed manifests.
- Conditional acceptance for retained data beyond default requires billing/contract amendment for Hosted customers. For Dedicated/Private customers this is a configuration change with operational cost covered under reserved capacity.

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-retention-playbooks

Olga Petrov
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Data Governance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sig_response_draft.docx (docx, 2 pages); proposed_export_schedule.csv (csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Voss <lvoss@quantumhealth.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention & erasure: customer-specific log policy for Quantum Health — proposed response

Laura — thanks for the clear asks and the SIG packet. We reviewed internally and can accommodate Quantum Health's requests with the following binding commitments and controls: 

1) Retention carveout: Redwood will configure a tenant-specific retention window of 180 days for debug/audit logs. For hosted customers, this requires a signed amendment reflecting incremental storage billing; for Dedicated/Private customers the change will be applied without extra per-token billing but may affect capacity planning.

2) Targeted deletion: Redwood will perform targeted erasure for tenant-scoped data within 30 calendar days of an authorized request (CS-approved). Evidence provided post-deletion will include a signed deletion manifest (object IDs, tenant IDs, deletion timestamps) and compaction job run logs. We will attach the manifest and logs to the customer's secure evidence portal.

3) Forensic snapshot export: Redwood commits to a 7-calendar-day delivery SLA for forensic exports up to a 72-hour time window from the request time. Exports will be delivered as NDJSON bundles with an index manifest and delivery checksum. Requests outside the 72-hour window or requiring expedited assembly may incur an acceleration fee and extended timelines.

Operational notes: we will add explicit language to the Sig/Caiq responses to clarify these caveats and suggested compensating controls for auditors (encrypted long-term storage, signed manifests). Diego / Olga — please review the draft in sig_response_draft.docx; Laura, I'm happy to walk through the evidence artifacts and timeline with your audit lead on a short call.

If this is acceptable, next action is: 1) Laura confirms acceptance of our proposed terms, 2) we route to CS to raise the configuration change ticket and billing amendment if hosted, and 3) we schedule a 30-minute call with your audit lead to confirm artifact formats.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sig_response_draft.docx (docx); proposed_export_schedule.csv (csv)
